messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: abnormal kv_cache key cardinality growth on prod-cluster-3, detection rule kv-prefix-explosion triggered (p95 keys/min > 10x baseline)
ops-bot: Incident severity: P1 (auto-escalate). Paging eng-runtime + oncall-sre.
oncall-sre: I’m on it — looking at the dashboard now. Can someone paste the recent batch config changes?
morgan: I rolled a batching tweak earlier this morning (PR #3456) that lowered max_batch_window_ms from 20 -> 50 and bumped continuous_batching=true for prefix routing. Reverting if needed.
nashish: @morgan (typo?), I think you mean ashish. I see a big increase in average batch size and CPU on kv-shard-12. Logs show many PUTs with extremely long prefix keys (some >4k chars).
julia: Observed tokenizer mismatch in the audit logs: some keys include raw template placeholders like "{{user_prompt}}" instead of tokenized placeholders. Looks like a template drift + hashing mismatch.
eva: Timeline: 10:03 deploy (batching change), 10:27 metric spike, 10:31 first customer 502, 10:34 automated throttles fired.
sam: Running quick grep on recent kv writes:
```
grep -E "prefix_key=|template=\"\{\{" /var/log/kv-writes.log | tail -n 50
```
sam: Lots of entries where tokenization step returned empty array then fallback wrote raw strings -> different hash space. That explains cardinality blowout.
oncall-sre: Can we triage impact? Which customers are hitting long sequences?
support-alex: Support reports 4 customers with elevated errors (inc. acme-corp prod), latency 5-10x for chat sessions > 1024 tokens. No data leak reported, just errors/timeouts.
morgan: Plan: 1) revert PR #3456 (batching) to stop extra aggregation pressure 2) run prefix cache scrub script to drop keys with obviously malformed prefixes 3) hotpatch tokenizer guard to reject raw-template placeholders before hashing 4) throttle continuous_batching via runtime flag.
nashish: Preparing revert now. Deploy-bot, can you run the rollback?
deploy-bot: Starting rollback of PR #3456 to prod-cluster-3 (canary first). Deploy link: https://deploys/redwood/rollback/3456
ops-bot: Canary rollback started on host pool p3-canary-2. Monitoring metrics.
ops-bot: Metric update: kv_write_rate falling after canary rollback, but high cardinality still persists in older shards.
sam: Cache scrub command ready (dry-run):
```
# list keys with malformed prefixes (preview)
python tools/kv_scan.py --prefix-regex "\{\{.*\}\}" --preview
# purge keys (careful):
python tools/kv_scan.py --prefix-regex "\{\{.*\}\}" --delete --confirm
```
julia: Recommend running scrub on a single shard first, then scale. We'll +1 on dry-run.
oncall-sre: I'll run scrub dry-run on shard-12 now.
ops-bot: scrub dry-run complete: ~14k candidate keys on shard-12, estimated memory reclaim 1.2GB. No immediate tail-latency regression in canary.
morgan: After canary looks good, apply global rollback and then run deletes shard-by-shard overnight. Also applying temporary throttle: set CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_ENABLED=false via config service.
deploy-bot: Global rollback completed at 10:56. CONTINUOUS_BATCHING_ENABLED set to false for prod-cluster-3.
ops-bot: Post-rollback metrics: average batch size back to baseline, CPU usage dropping, but prefix-key cardinality decays slowly.
support-alex: Notifying affected customers with ETA for mitigation and postmortem. Draft msg: "We're seeing increased errors for long chat sessions due to keying bug; we've rolled back batching config and are purging malformed keys; expect recovery in 4-8 hours." Anyone edit?
eva: Add note: 'no user data exfiltration suspected; writes only malformed keys.'
oncall-sre: Handoff: I need to step off for the next meeting. Paging oncall @ashish for ongoing scrub and customer comms.
nashish: I’m taking over. Will run shard-by-shard delete windows starting 02:00 UTC, rate-limited to avoid inducing IO spikes. Will also deploy a tokenizer guard hotfix (small check to normalize tokens before hashing). PR target: #3472.
morgan: Thx. Please capture rollforward steps: re-enable continuous batching only after thorough regression tests and keyspace stabilization.
support-alex: Will update status page and ticket 8732. Customers informed.
oncall-sre: Closing paging loop for now — ops monitoring on standby. Resume if error rate > 2% or any new errors.
ops-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Mitigations applied: batching rollback, continuous_batching disabled, cache scrub dry-run completed, scrub schedule set. Owning team: eng-runtime + eng-ml (ashish, julia, morgan).
nashish: I'm logging this as a postmortem candidate. Primary root cause: batching config + tokenizer/template drift producing unnormalized prefixes and unexpected hash churn leading to KV cache blowup and perf cliff.
morgan: Thanks all — handing to next oncall for nightwatch.
support-alex: Next steps for postmortem: reproduce locally with long-template cases, add unit test that rejects raw-template placeholders in prefix hashing, and add metric to alert on tokenizer-fallback-rate.
ops-bot: Incident P1 transitioned to monitoring at 11:02.
sam: leaving one more note: command snippets, logs and scrub results saved under /var/incidents/2955554321/ for the postmortem.
ejournal: (automated) incident-thread archived to internal bucket.
